title: MetricsPing — Blocked, Technically
objective: MetricsPing refuses to ping 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1' by name. Reach a simulated service listening on loopback anyway.

verifier.condition: A request is sent to a loopback address although its ORIGINAL, unparsed host string was neither 'localhost' nor '127.0.0.1'.

weakness: The blocklist compares the raw, unparsed input string against a short list of known-bad spellings of loopback, but the underlying URL parser accepts several other numeric encodings of the exact same address that the blocklist never anticipated.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /ping (url field; the raw string is blocklist-checked, then parsed and fetched separately)
seededData: A simulated service listening on 127.0.0.1:9100 representing an unauthenticated internal metrics endpoint.
hints: Confirm the obvious spellings really are blocked first: try 'localhost' and '127.0.0.1' directly.
An IPv4 address is normally written as four decimal numbers, but that's just one way to write the same number. Computers don't care about the spelling.
Try an IPv4 address written as a single decimal number, or in hexadecimal, instead of the usual dotted form.
burpNotes: Send a request with the url parameter set to an alternate numeric encoding of 127.0.0.1 (decimal, hex, or octal) — none of these strings match the blocklist's exact comparisons.
